channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Video Understanding vs Image Classification: The Extra Axis
item.description: Time is not just another axis. It breaks independence assumptions, inflates apparent accuracy, and demands leakage-aware splits that most video pipelines quietly skip.

item.title: Optical Character Recognition: From Pipelines to Deep Nets
item.description: A tour through classical OCR pipelines and the specific failure modes that end-to-end deep learning actually solved, not just automated.

item.title: Anomaly Detection in Vision: One-Class Methods Made Simple
item.description: Most defects are rare and unlabelled. One-class methods learn what normal looks like, then flag anything that does not fit, no anomaly examples required.

item.title: Convolutional Networks Versus Vision Transformers, Honestly
item.description: CNNs and ViTs both work well on images, but they fail differently under small data and distribution shift. I compare them with a concrete worked example.

item.title: Catastrophic Forgetting: What Fine-Tuning Quietly Overwrites
item.description: Fine-tuning can boost your target metric while quietly erasing older capabilities. Here is how to notice and measure the damage.

item.title: Fine-Tuning on Small Data: When Does It Actually Help
item.description: How to tell whether fine-tuning on a small dataset is actually working, or whether you are just chasing noise in your validation split.

item.title: Instruction Tuning versus Fine-Tuning: The Real Difference
item.description: Fine-tuning specialises a model for one task. Instruction tuning teaches it to follow tasks it has never seen. Confusing the two skews evaluation.

item.title: Continuous Retraining on a Schedule Can Be a Trap
item.description: A retraining cadence is not a monitoring strategy. Here is why scheduled retraining can mask drift, hide bugs, and quietly erode trust in your pipeline.

item.title: MLOps for a Team of One: What to Automate First
item.description: You cannot automate everything as a solo practitioner. Here is the order that actually saves time: data checks, then retraining, then serving, then monitoring.

item.title: Setting Up Your First MLOps Project on a Laptop
item.description: Cloud infrastructure will not fix a badly designed pipeline. Build the habits first, on your laptop, then scale.

item.title: Interview Questions for MLOps Roles: What They Really Test
item.description: MLOps interviews rarely test frameworks. They test whether you understand failure, reproducibility, and who gets paged at 3am.

item.title: Evaluation Harnesses for Prompts: Treat Them Like Models
item.description: Prompt edits change behaviour just like model swaps do. Here is why they deserve the same evaluation discipline.

item.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting: When It Helps, When It Hurts
item.description: Chain-of-thought prompting boosts performance on some tasks and quietly degrades it on others. I unpack the mechanism, a worked example, and when to skip it.

item.title: System Prompts vs User Prompts: Where Instructions Belong
item.description: System prompts and user prompts are not interchangeable containers. Where you put an instruction changes how reliably a model follows it.

item.title: Few-Shot Prompts: How Many Examples Is Too Many
item.description: Adding more few-shot examples feels safe, but past a point it wastes tokens, biases outputs, and can quietly hurt accuracy.

item.title: Structured Prompt Templates: Stop Guessing, Start Repeating
item.description: Ad hoc prompting doesn't scale. A structured template with fixed slots makes prompting testable, versionable, and far easier to debug.

item.title: Building a Case Study a Hiring Manager Will Actually Read
item.description: A hiring manager gives your portfolio ten seconds. Structure your case study so it earns the next ninety.

item.title: How Pretraining Data Shapes What a Transformer Can Do
item.description: Architecture gets the credit, but pretraining data quietly decides what a transformer can ever learn to do well.

item.title: Semantic Segmentation vs Object Detection: Pick Wisely
item.description: Segmentation and detection both find objects, but they cost and deliver very different things. Here is how to choose without guessing.

item.title: Data Scientist vs Machine Learning Engineer, in Practice
item.description: Same buzzwords, different jobs. Here's what actually separates data science from ML engineering once you look past the job title.
